name: Chicken Sajji
description: Balochistan-inspired whole chicken sajji with restrained seasoning, roasted steadily for a deeply browned exterior and juicy, fully cooked meat.
ingredients: 2 tbsp cooking oil or melted butter
method: Pat the whole chicken dry inside and out. Make only a few shallow cuts in the thickest fleshy areas so seasoning can reach the surface without cutting deeply into bone.
Mix the lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, salt, black pepper, cumin and crushed coriander, then rub the mixture evenly over and inside the chicken.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 45 minutes. Keep the raw bird chilled until you are ready to cook it.
Roast on a rotisserie, covered grill or in a preheated oven using steady heat. Turn or rotate as appropriate for the equipment so the whole bird browns evenly rather than scorching in one area.

Brush lightly with oil or melted butter during the later stage of roasting. Continue until the thickest breast and inner-thigh areas are fully cooked; use a reliable doneness check and avoid touching bone when measuring.
Remove from the heat and rest for about 10 minutes before carving so the juices settle, then serve hot with lemon wedges, rice or naan.
tips: Whole chickens cook more evenly when allowed to roast steadily rather than over excessively high heat.
Use a food thermometer in the thickest areas to confirm doneness, especially with a whole bird.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate covered and reheat only the portion needed until thoroughly hot.
